result.topic_en: The page finishes an interpolation computing an astronomical longitude for x = 24 1/2 and compares it with the Connaissance des Temps, then begins section IV on summing a series of sines divided by products of half-difference sines, using complex exponentials.

IV. Summation der Reihe

$\frac{\sin(na+k)}{\sin\frac{1}{2}(a-b)\sin\frac{1}{2}(a-c)\sin\frac{1}{2}(a-d)\ldots} + \frac{\sin(nb+k)}{\sin\frac{1}{2}(b-a)\sin\frac{1}{2}(b-c)\sin\frac{1}{2}(b-d)\ldots} + \frac{\sin(nc+k)}{\sin\frac{1}{2}(c-a)\sin\frac{1}{2}(c-b)\sin\frac{1}{2}(c-d)\ldots}$
$+ \text{etc.} = S$

Die erforderliche Beschaffenheit von n wird im Laufe der Untersuchung selbst angegeben.
Man setze [-sin-] $\sqrt{-1} = i$, $\cos a + i\sin a = A$, $\cos b + i \sin b = B$, $\cos c + i\sin c = C$ etc.
Alsdann ist $\sin\frac{1}{2}(a-b) = \frac{A-B}{2i(\cos\frac{1}{2}(a+b)}$

$A - B = 2i\sin\frac{1}{2}(a-b)\{\cos\frac{1}{2}(a+b) + i\sin\frac{1}{2}(a+b)\}$
$A - C = 2i\sin\frac{1}{2}(a-c)\{\cos\frac{1}{2}(a+c) + i\sin\frac{1}{2}(a+c)\}$
$A - D = 2i\sin\frac{1}{2}(a-d)\{\cos\frac{1}{2}(a+d) + i\sin\frac{1}{2}(a+d)\}$
etc.

folglich $(A-B)(A-C)(A-D)\ldots = (2i)^{m-1}\sin\frac{1}{2}(a-b)\sin\frac{1}{2}(a-c)\sin\frac{1}{2}(a-d)\ldots \times \{\cos\frac{1}{2}(a+b+c+d\ldots+(m-2)a) + i\sin\frac{1}{2}(a+b+c+d\ldots+(m-2)a)\}$
